text:
alert-bot: PROD: Increased 504 / 502 spike on hosted inference gateway for tenant 'acme-corp' — 2m avg error rate 18% :rotating_light:
ashwin: seeing same, grafana shows scale-up backlog on inference-pool-us-east-1, queue length jumped at 18:42 :eyes:
maya: customer cs pinged, they're hitting api timeouts on batch ingest flows, raised to priority P1 by liz-cs :point_up_2:
liz-cs: customer reporting 30s client-side timeouts and retries. asked for timeline + repro steps, they sent curl that times out consistently. they want mitigation now.
jon: quick snapshot from logs — gateway returning 502s while backend pods still initializing (long init logs). suspect HPA/KEDA interaction where KEDA metric scrape delay + KEDA cool-down prevents immediate pod warmups.
ashwin: can someone paste scaledobject and hpa status? I want to see lastScaleTime and cooldowns.
jon: paste below (redacted):
```
$ kubectl -n prod get scaledobject inference-worker -o yaml
triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      serverAddress: http://prom-prom:9090
      metricName: inference_queue_length
      threshold: "50"
cooldownPeriod: "300"
```
and HPA: lastScaleTime 18:40, desiredReplicas 2, currentReplicas 0, conditions: ScalingActive False (metrics delayed)
sre-oncall: wait, desired 2 but current 0? that means pods are still in Pending/ContainerCreating. Any image pull or init logs?
jon: init logs show heavy model fetch and quantization step taking ~14s per model, but probe/readiness waits for KV cache init and then warms batcher. startup sequence is ~45s on current nodes.
maya: so we have 0->2 target but warmstart is ~45s, and client timeouts at 30s — mismatch. also KEDA cooldown 300s prevents additional rapid scaling if metrics flap. combination -> repeated 504s.
nashwin: that's the problem: operator-level cooldown + long model init -> requests stuck. For short bursts we need a different approach: prewarming or aggressive burst pool.
liz-cs: customer wants immediate mitigation and ETA. any quick workaround?
sre-oncall: mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase HPA minReplicas to 2 (avoid 0). 2) reduce KEDA cooldown to 30s (risk of flapping). 3) enable prewarm/pod-standby for that tenant if we have per-tenant pools.
jon: I ran quick kube patch to set minReplicas=2 for inference-worker in prod for acme-corp namespace, also bumped readinessProbe initialDelay to 5s to allow early traffic proxies — rolling now. deploy-bot: deployment inference-worker scaled to 2 replicas (requested by jon) :white_check_mark:
alert-bot: traffic error rate dropped to 3% in 90s, latency median improved.
maya: log snippet from gateway during incident: 
```
2025-11-05T18:42:31Z gateway ERROR proxy: upstream request failed: dial tcp 10.244.2.12:8080: connect: connection refused
2025-11-05T18:42:34Z gateway WARN request id=abc123 took 31.2s -> client timeout
```
jon: repro instructions for SRE/devs:
1) simulate burst: for i in {1..150}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"ping"}' & done
2) watch keda metrics: kubectl -n prod get prometheusrules or prom query `inference_queue_length`
3) observe scaledobject cooldown and HPA desired/current mismatch
ashwin: root cause summary: KEDA configured with long cooldown (300s) + HPA minReplicas=0 + model init/warmup > client timeout => scale-up lag causes gateway 5xx/timeouts. compounded by scaling suppression on KEDA when metrics oscillate.
liz-cs: told customer we've put minReplicas=2 temporarily and are working on a long-term fix, they acknowledged but want timeline for permanent solution.
sre-oncall: long-term remediation ideas: set tenant-specific prewarm pools, decouple control-plane cooldown from cold-start metric (separate metric for sustained vs burst), implement async ingress with queued responses / retry header, and reduce model init time (lazy load smaller shard first).
maya: action items assigned:
- ashwin: evaluate KEDA cooldown reduction and safe thresholds (owner)
- jon: instrument model init time and introduce warm-cache probe for readiness (owner)
- ops: draft runbook for emergency minReplica bump and communicate to CS (owner: liz-cs)
- eng-runtime: investigate faster warmstart path (quantization lazy load)
all: please update thread when done. :thumbsup:
jon: leaving exact command I used to bump minReplicas in case of followup:
```bash
kubectl -n prod patch scaledobject inference-worker --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicaCount","value":2}]'
```
nashwin: I'll follow up with a short doc recommending default cooldowns and a canary for per-tenant prewarm.
liz-cs: customer responded: "Thanks, latency is back to normal. We'll keep monitoring." closing P1 but wanting postmortem.
alert-bot: incident closed (recovered) — duration 18m.
